Inject | src/routes/reports.js:16 | The `status` query parameter is concatenated into the SQL of `GET /reports`. Any user can read every row of every table. | Entry: any holder of a valid session (the only gate is `requireUser`, `src/server.js:31-32`) sends `GET /reports?status=...`. Path: `src/server.js:33` copies `url.searchParams` into `req.query` and nothing validates it. At `src/routes/reports.js:16` the raw value goes inside `'...'` in the SQL string. At `src/db.js:8` `db.prepare(sql)` compiles the full string, so only `user.id` is bound and nothing escapes `status`. Effect: `status=x' OR 1=1 --` returns the reports of all owners. `status=x' UNION SELECT token, user_id, expires_at, 0 FROM sessions --` returns live session tokens of other users, which is a full account takeover through `src/auth.js:7-10`. Guard: at `src/routes/reports.js:16`, use `AND status = ?` and push `req.query.status` into the params array.

Cross | src/routes/reports.js:36 | The `file` query parameter of `GET /reports/export` is joined to the export path with no containment. Any user can read any file that the process can read. | Entry: any holder of a valid session sends `GET /reports/export?file=...`. Path: `src/server.js:33` gives the raw `req.query.file`. `src/routes/reports.js:36` runs `path.join(EXPORTS, String(user.id), file)`. `path.join` resolves `..` segments but does not keep the result under `EXPORTS/<id>`. Nothing checks the prefix. `src/routes/reports.js:38` `fs.createReadStream(file)` opens the file and pipes it to the response. Effect: `file=../2/<name>` reads the exports of another user. `file=../../reports.db` (the default `REPORTS_DB` sits next to the default `exports` folder, `src/db.js:3`, `src/routes/reports.js:7`) downloads the whole database with all reports, users and session tokens. `file=../../../../etc/passwd` and similar reads any file on the host. Guard: at `src/routes/reports.js:36`, take `path.resolve` of the joined path and refuse it unless it starts with `path.join(EXPORTS, String(user.id)) + path.sep`. Or keep only `path.basename(file)`.

Access | src/routes/reports.js:62 | `DELETE /reports/:id` deletes a report by its id alone with no check of the owner. Any user can delete the reports of other users. | Entry: any holder of a valid session sends `DELETE /reports/<n>`. Ids are sequential integers (`(\d+)`, `src/routes/reports.js:60`), so they are easy to guess. Path: `src/server.js:31-36` makes sure only that some session exists. `src/routes/reports.js:62` runs `DELETE FROM reports WHERE id = ?` with only `match[1]` bound and no `owner` condition. The sibling routes include the owner check: `src/server.js:21` for projects and `src/routes/reports.js:48` for the cover. Effect: a user can delete every report of every other user, one id after another. Guard: at `src/routes/reports.js:62`, add `AND owner = ?` with `user.id`.

count: 3

I checked these and found no hole:
- **`/reports/search` regex** (`src/routes/reports.js:25`): an attacker can supply the pattern, but the lens excludes attacker data in a regex and ReDoS. The rows are already limited to the owner.
- **`convert` in `execFile`** (`src/routes/reports.js:50-54`): no shell runs. The font comes from the deployment's environment. `report.id` is an integer that the owner check already confirmed.
